newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwifruit NZ opposes Tauranga Intl airport plan.
newsitem.headline: Kiwifruit NZ opposes Tauranga Intl airport plan.

text.p: Kiwifruit New Zealand chairman John Palmer said on Tuesday he supported local fruitgrowers in their opposition to a proposed international airport for Tauranga.
Palmer told the Kiwifruit New Zealand annual meeting the fruitfly outbreak in Auckland last year was a timely reminder of the risks to the industry.
"The risk to the kiwifruit industry of a potential fruitfly outbreak from international passengers disembarking in Tauranga is too great to even contemplate," he said.
"Such an outbreak in Tauranga at any time when the crop is on the vine would have disastrous consequences for this industry," he said.
Kiwifruit New Zealand, formerly the New Zealand Kiwifruit Marketing Board, split off its marketing role to Zespri International early this year.
New Zealand represents about 30 percent of the world's kiwifruit production, much of it from the Bay of Plenty region.
